newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Wrangles hit African First Ladies' club.
newsitem.headline: Wrangles hit African First Ladies' club.

text.p: Wrangles have hit a club of First Ladies from the Organisation of African Unity established just weeks ago to help promote peace and unity.

Zimbabwe state news agency ZIANA reported on Tuesday that there were disagreements over the chairship of the Africa First Ladies Peace Mission, currently held by Nigerian First Lady Maryam Abacha, wife of military strongman Sani Abacha.
The agency said some First Ladies, including Nana Rawlings of Ghana, accused Abacha of hijacking the cause to promote the interests of the military regime of her husband.
Abacha denied the charge, saying: "I am not personalising anything, I am even trying to rotate the leadership in the same manner as the OAU chairmanship.
"Even at yesterday's (Monday) meeting I asked what the other Ladies wished to do about the chairmanship and as you noticed, they did not want to talk which means they are happy".
Rawlings alleged Abacha failed to arrange a meeting to elect office bearers.
"We were supposed to have met as a bureau...but it did not happen because things were not at all organised," she said.
The club was formed in Nigeria last month to help promote peace and unity on the troubled African continent.
